prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · REST endpoints (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Endpoint" · longest unbreakable word 261px · one-line width 261px
  col 2: header "Method" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 55px
  col 3: header "Auth" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 46px
  col 4: header "Rate limit" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 85px · one-line width 670px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 762px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 761px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r0A: widths [282, 76, 67, 89, 247] · table 762×415px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 60, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [282, 95, 95, 95, 194] · table 762×461px · row heights [36, 129, 106, 60, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [282, 105, 90, 110, 174] · table 762×508px · row heights [36, 153, 129, 60, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r0A"],"acceptable":["r0B"],"bad":[{"design":"r0C","why":"Three columns of near-trivial content (Method, Auth, Rate limit) are padded to 90–110px while the only text-heavy column, Description, is squeezed to 153px of text and breaks to 6 lines, producing ragged short lines ('Returns the public / profile of a user, / including display / name…') and inflating the table to 508px tall for no informational gain."}],"contrast":{"widths":[152,152,152,153,152],"why":"The tidy-looking 'equal columns' solution: it looks balanced in the abstract, but a 261px endpoint identifier forced into 131px of text splits mid-word across several lines, destroying the one thing the reader must copy verbatim, and it still leaves Description cramped."},"ranges":[[282,300],[76,96],[67,92],[89,110],[238,262]],"rationale":"Endpoint is a hard-constrained identifier column: its longest token is 261px, so 282px is a floor, and every pixel above it is wasted. Method, Auth and Rate limit hold short, fixed vocabulary (GET/POST/DELETE, Bearer/Admin, 600/min) whose one-line widths are 55/46/68px, so their minimums (76/67/89) are also near their ideal. That frees the entire remainder for Description, the only column whose line count actually drives row height — r0A gives it 247px and holds the tallest cell to 4 lines. r0B is defensible as slightly airier, but the 19px it adds to Method and 28px to Auth buy no content and cost Description a line in two rows; r0C spends the budget the wrong way entirely.","principles":{"general":["Give each column the width of its longest unbreakable token first; distribute the surplus to the column with the most prose, since that is the column that sets row height.","Never let an identifier column (path, key, code) wrap: the cost of a mid-word split is paid on every row and every copy-paste, and it dwarfs any aesthetic gain from symmetry.","Symmetry and equal widths are not neutral defaults; on tables with heterogeneous content they actively misallocate space from long-text columns to short-code columns."],"specific":["Method/Auth/Rate limit are effectively fixed-width categorical columns here; their minimums (76/67/89) are also their practical optimum, so all the design decision lives in the Endpoint/Description split.","The endpoint /api/v1/exports/{jobId}/download at 261px pins the Endpoint column and leaves only ~479px to be divided four ways, which makes this a zero-sum width problem rather than a breathing-room problem."]},"tradeoffs":"r0A sits exactly at the minimum for Method (76px = 'Method' header width) and Rate limit (89px = header width), so it has no slack against font fallback or zoom; a designer who values robustness over compactness would pick r0B and accept two extra line-wraps in Description. Some readers also find the three minimum-width columns visually cramped next to the very wide Endpoint column, even though the content justifies it.","uncertain":"Whether the near-zero slack in r0A's Method column is acceptable in production rendering (subpixel/font variance could wrap the header), and whether a slightly wider Description (240–260) with Endpoint relaxed to ~290 reads better than the exact-minimum allocation."}
